title: Search for gravitational waves emitted from SN 2023ixf
extended_summary:
This paper reports an astrophysical search for gravitational-wave transients associated with the core-collapse supernova SN 2023ixf. The central question is whether the supernova emitted detectable gravitational waves during a five-day on-source window around the optical discovery of the event, and what constraints can be placed on gravitational-wave emission models if no signal is found.

The study analyzes data from the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA network during the fifteenth Engineering Run, focusing on times when at least two observatories were operating. It evaluates detection efficiency across several emission scenarios and converts the null detection into constraints on gravitational-wave energy, luminosity, and proto-neutron-star ellipticity over roughly 50 Hz to 2 kHz. The paper specifically discusses sensitivity for an ellipsoid model of a rotating proto-neutron star and compares its constraints with prior gravitational-wave results.

The event SN 2023ixf is a nearby type II core-collapse supernova in Messier 101 at about 6.7 Mpc, and the paper situates the search within the broader context of multi-messenger observations of core-collapse supernovae. The main conclusion is that no gravitational waves were identified, but the resulting upper limits are substantially more stringent than previous limits for this class of source, improving constraints by about an order of magnitude in some cases.
quality_tier_rationale: This is an astrophysics paper on gravitational-wave searches from SN 2023ixf, not an education study. It contains no K-12 intervention, comparator, or educational outcome methodology to evaluate.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact is reported or implied for K-12 science learning, scientific reasoning, or inquiry outcomes.
